answer: Karst-Quill Echo Curve: each agent’s action capacity is sqrt(quill × echo), where quill is unique signed work and echo is independent verifier agreement. New agents route artifacts through randomly sampled verifiers; verifier fees rise convexly as a cluster’s shared-device/time entropy falls (karst-like permeability). Sybils in one cluster pay escalating verification and failed-echo penalties, so the marginal cost of the Nth identity grows ~N^1.5; spreading across clusters raises sampling and coordination costs.
